replies.author: aaravchen
replies.text:
I believe this is a Schwab issue. It broke for me while on Stock still and stayed broken as I went to CalyxOS and now GrapheneOS. There's also near continuous reports in Reddit that it's broken on Stock OS as well.

Schwab is the only US bank that supports Zelle that doesn't have web access to it (app only), which speaks to their lack of sophistication. Someone on Reddit I believe also did debugging of the app and found they were making nonsense requests that looked like they came from someone ignorantly trying to patch in a very old out of date SDK-built applet.

Given that in the US, FedNow has also been coming for a few years and almost every major bank except Schwab is on the public list for being at least in the process of implementing it (there's a bank-to-bank API first, then a customer to customer API after most bank-to-bank is rolled out that will replace the Wells Fargo-led private Zelle), it seems like they're probably half-assing it and dragging their feet since historically they've been using their checking accounts as a draw to get people to use their brokerage accounts and have tended to target older generations that don't prioritize such features.

I know personally I've looked at other banks specifically because of these types of issues, and the only alternatives are scammy internet-only banks, and huge high fee legacy banks that keep getting caught stealing customer's money by illegally signing they up for extra services without approval and getting off with a fine of <0.1% of the profit they made doing it.

replies.author: SipCoffee
replies.text:
Steps to Fix Schwab Zelle

​Go to Settings > Apps > See all apps > Schwab.

​Tap Permissions > Contacts and change the setting to either Allow or Don't allow (do not leave it on limited/ask every time).

​Under the main Schwab App Info page, scroll down to Exploit Protection and toggle Exploit Protection Compatibility Mode to On.

​Force stop the Schwab app and reopen it.

replies.author: aaravchen
replies.text:
SipCoffee

These are the same steps everyone's been trying for the 3+ years it's been broken, but you're right that it is working now (withoit the Exploit Compatibility being needed). Excellent news!

Schwab has had broken Zelle in thier android app for almost 3 years across amlost all Android devices. It hasn't been limited or unique to GrapheneOS. You can dig thru Reddit to confirm.

Someone did a debug investigation a while ago and thier judgment was that someone paid a crappy contractor to integrate the mandatory premade Zelle plugin into the Schwab app, and the contractor did it very wrong. Which caused it to be really slow and break a lot (if it even worked).

Unfortunately Schwab is also the only bank that "supports Zelle" that doesn't have Zelle integration on thier website, so unlike every other bank, you can only access sending money thru thier iOS or Android app and don't have any backup solution if that fails.

replies.author: DeletedUser1090
replies.text:
I no longer use Schwab Bank due to a parent hiring a Schwab advisor on a lump sum, so I moved to E*Trade/Morgan Stanley Private Bank. I have no issues with E*Trade despite using the same bolted-on Zelle plug-in.

Although E*Trade has worse customer support than Schwab, it is an option if you don't mind transferring your cash, assets and direct deposit for working Zelle and higher bank interest.

Chase also works if you have >150K in assets for "private client" or are okay without perks like free ATMs if otherwise, aren't an advanced investor/trader, or need branches, etc. Chase has it's faults but has an actual good Zelle implementation.

Source: I have both CPC and E*Trade/MSPB.

replies.author: DeletedUser1090

aaravchen I'd suggest moving to E*Trade if you need Zelle. However, E*Trade support is worse than Schwab.

If you are purely buy-and-hold and have >100K in assets or don't need unlimited ATM withdrawals, Bank of America/Merrill Lynch is an option. At >150K in assets, Chase is an option too.
